transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Start: 09:43 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Luca Moreno (Redwood SE), Elena Royce (NimbusGrid Head Partnerships), Markus Hsu (NimbusGrid Lead Infra), Priya Anand (NimbusGrid VP Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Redwood and NimbusGrid did a partner intro covering channel motions, GPU integration possibilities, and basic security/compliance fit. NimbusGrid is a systems integrator and reseller focused on edge + hybrid GPU deployment for enterprise customers; they're exploring integrating Redwood's runtime as a turnkey inference option on their managed hardware + to resell Redwood Dedicated/Private offerings. Action items defined: deck exchange, infra spec, and scheduling technical deep-dive.

Topics noted: partner program structure, co-sell models, certified GPU SKUs, private deployment networking, KMS/HSM, SOC2, demo/benchmark plan, marketplace listing, technical integration checklist.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'm Samira, AE at Redwood, and with me is Luca our solution engineer.
[00:12] Elena: Hi, Elena here, Head of Cloud Partnerships at NimbusGrid. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:16] Markus: Markus, infra lead. Looking forward to learning how Redwood could fit into our managed GPU offering.
[00:24] Priya: Priya here, product. Short on time so I'll probably listen most of the call but want to understand GTM and what customers we'd target.
[00:33] Luca: Awesome. We'll keep it crisp. The goal today is to run through partner program basics, what integration points look like from an infra side, and surface any immediate blockers — like security or SKU compatibility.
[00:45] Samira: Yes. Quick background on NimbusGrid would help, Elena?
[00:49] Elena: Sure, we're a channel-first MSP, we manage GPU clusters across colo and edge sites for regulated customers — financial services and healthcare, mostly. We do both resell and systems integration; recently we've had demand for a turn-key inference stack. Folks ask for low latency, private deployments, and predictable costs.
[01:10] Samira: Great. That aligns pretty well with Redwood Dedicated and Private. We offer a hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC/on-prem packages. For partner scenarios, there are a few common patterns: 1) reseller + managed deployment where Redwood supplies the control plane and model catalog, 2) private deployment where the customer or partner runs control plane with Redwood software, and 3) hybrid where control plane is shared but compute runs in partner infra.
[01:42] Markus: On the private side, our main concerns are networking — how does VPC peering, or cross-account routing, work, and what about KMS? We need to ensure keys never leave our HSMs.
[01:56] Luca: Totally. We support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations; you can provision keys in your HSM and Redwood's runtime will use those via a KMS bridge. There's some work in the ops runbook for cert rotation and least-privilege IAM roles. We'll put a checklist together.
[02:12] Elena: Also compliance — customers care about SOC2 and audit logs. Do you have SOC2 reports and per-token auditability?
[02:20] Samira: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II; we can share the attestation. Our Console exposes token-level usage and per-route logs which customers can forward to SIEMs over secure connectors. We'll drop links. (link: https://redwood.ai/partners/deck)
[02:33] Priya: On GTM, are you expecting revenue share, referral, or co-sell?
[02:38] Samira: We have flexible programs — referral fees for pure resell, higher share and co-marketing when the partner owns onboarding and runbook. For strategic partners we do joint pipeline commits and MDF. I'll send the partner program overview after this call.
[02:51] Elena: Good. For technical depth: Markus will lead; we want to see a runthrough of how model artifacts are deployed to your runtime, can we ship quantized artifacts, and what the lifecycle looks like?
[03:05] Luca: At a high level, model artifacts are stored in a registry (OCI-compatible) and the runtime pulls them. We support quantized weights and multi-precision artifacts. For Dedicated/Private we support pinned model versions and can deploy via an operator or a deployment API. We also surface performance profiles so you can choose a kernel/quant setting that meets throughput/latency SLOs.
[03:31] Markus: When you say registry, is that an internal Redwood registry or can we use our private container registry? Some of our enterprise customers require images stay in their repo.
[03:40] Luca: You can use your own registry. The runtime pulls from private registries using credentials we configure in the deployment. We'll document the CRI creds flow.
[03:49] Elena: Pricing — high level, how do partners resell Dedicated capacity? Is it a markup model or reseller SKU?
[03:56] Samira: Both. For early pilots we often do fixed-price commits to simplify procurement; for broader programs partners resell SKUs with recommended list prices. We'll share example pricing and margin bands.
[04:09] Priya: Any marketplace options? Could we list a managed offering in a cloud marketplace for customers to discover?
[04:14] Samira: Yes, marketplace listing is possible particularly for Dedicated and Private. There are some requirements per cloud provider but we can collaborate on listing assets.
[04:23] Markus: Networking specifics — what's the typical VPC architecture? Do you support private link, direct connect, or do you expect NAT egress?
[04:33] Luca: We support VPC peering, PrivateLink-style endpoints for control plane comms, and direct connect for high throughput links. For on-prem we do a VPN or direct circuit. There is a small amount of control-plane egress for telemetry if you choose hosted control plane — can be limited or routed through customer's egress.
[04:52] Elena: On security again, SSO and RBAC — we need SAML/SCIM for user provisioning in the console.
[04:59] Samira: SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported in the Console; RBAC can be mapped to roles. For partner-managed tenants we can extend roles and federated access.
[05:11] Markus: Operationally, how do updates happen? We need a maintenance window so our customers don't see cold-starts or evictions during business hours.
[05:20] Luca: We support configurable maintenance windows and can do canaries and gradual rollouts. For Dedicated we can schedule rolling updates per-host to avoid mass restarts; for Private we hand over the update ops runbook and can consult.
[05:33] Elena: Benchmarks — our sales team will want latency and throughput numbers we can show. Do you have public numbers or a benchmark kit?
[05:40] Samira: We publish verified performance profiles and can run a joint benchmark. Our Optimize toolkit can help pick batch sizes and quantization to hit targets. We'll propose a pilot benchmark: 3 models, 1k qps baseline, and a latency tail study.
[05:56] Priya: Who owns support for managed deployments sold by NimbusGrid? Do you offer white-glove support to partners?
[06:03] Samira: We have partner support tiers. For co-managed customers we offer L2/L3 support via a partner SLA. For white-glove we can include a named SE and faster SLAs as part of the package.
[06:14] Markus: One tricky area is GPU SKU compatibility — e.g., Hopper vs Ada vs older amps. We have customers on mixed GPU fleets and want to know which models and quantizations map to which cards.
[06:26] Luca: We'll share a compatibility matrix. In practice we target a set of certified SKUs for each model family; we also provide fallbacks — for example lower precision options for older GPUs. The runtime auto-selects the best kernel for the detected architecture.
[06:43] Elena: For go-to-market, we'd like a co-branded quickstart for new customers where NimbusGrid handles onboarding and Redwood provides the runtime. How long to get a new tenant up and running?
[06:54] Samira: For a standard Dedicated tenant with basic models, we can onboard 2-4 weeks. Private/on-prem is longer depending on network and approvals — 4-8 weeks commonly.
[07:05] Priya: Ok that's reasonable. Any legal / procurement flags? Data residency or indemnities?
[07:12] Samira: Our T&Cs cover standard data processing terms; for enterprise we do DPA and can contract specific residency clauses for Private. We'll surface typical contract timelines and redlines we see.
[07:22] Markus: On the technical dive we want to look at the operator you'd install on our infra — how it manages model lifecycle and secrets. Can Luca walk through the operator flow next time?
[07:32] Luca: Absolutely. I'll prepare an operator walkthrough: bootstrap, secret injection (KMS integration), model pull workflow, autoscaling hooks, and metrics exports.
[07:43] Elena: A couple of quick asks — 1) can you provide a sample revenue share model we can use in financials, 2) example support SLAs for partner-managed customers, and 3) a short checklist for SOC2 artifacts?
[07:57] Samira: Yes to all. We'll include those in the deck and a short checklist for your legal and sales teams.
[08:06] Priya: Last thing — marketplace listing requires security review for some clouds. Do you have a standard package for that?
[08:12] Samira: We do — marketplace listing artifacts, security attestation, deployment templates. We'll attach those assets to the follow-up email.
[08:20] Elena: Great. Let's talk about a pilot — small managed deployment on 8x A100-equivalent nodes for a healthcare customer, we estimate 3k GPU hours/month. Is that in scope?
[08:33] Luca: That sounds fine. For initial pilots we often recommend Dedicated reserved pool with a pilot commit to hit predictable costs, then convert to a reseller SKU. We can size the pool and recommend batch/kv cache settings to reduce token costs.
[08:50] Markus: KV cash — sorry, I mean KV cache — how does that impact memory footprint on the GPU? We have customers sensitive to footprint per-host.
[08:58] Luca: KV cache can add memory overhead per connection. We have options: shared cache for repeated prompts, or per-session caches with eviction policies. We can show memory estimates per-config in the deep-dive.
[09:12] Elena: Any blockers from our side to proceed to a technical deep-dive?
[09:16] Markus: We need a list of required network ports, the operator image spec, and KMS integration notes. Also sample SAML metadata for testing.
[09:25] Samira: We'll put that in the checklist. Luca will own the operator spec.
[09:30] Priya: Timeline-wise let's aim for the technical deep-dive in two weeks; sales and legal can review the deck this week.
[09:38] Samira: Works for us. I'll send the deck and partner program overview by 7/20. Luca will schedule the deep-dive.
[09:45] Elena: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the materials.
[09:48] Samira: Thanks — we'll follow up with next steps and a calendar invite for the deep-dive.

End of meeting.
